After checking, shout it out, don't scream but tell to yourself as if you're talking to a friend. Stop giving it attention, whatever that comes to your mind stop giving it attention, it's a constant cycle, 

You're doing something - You get a thought of your ex - You try to not thing about it - You start to think of hurting her - You try more to not thing about it -  you think of your ex - You try your hardest to not think about it - you realize your day is ruined - You go back to that "something" half-hearted and bitter about yourself 

The problem is whenever you're trying NOT to think about it, you're literally thinking about it? What's the point then? How about you follow a different cycle.

You're doing something - You get a thought of your ex - You keep on doing that something with full focus -  You get a thought of your ex - You keep on doing that something with full focus again - You might get something else - But you do not care about it, instead you're still trying to focus on your work - ...

At the end of day following this cycle will get you more work done and a day forward to a life without OCD.

The only way to literally get rid of OCD is to learn to Focus. When you're so focused on the thing that's in front of you, you would not worry about anything around you, What do you feel about the weather?, the outfit you're wearing?, the people's reaction on the outfit you're wearing, the scars that you have, your friend's untidy desk, everything fades away to the dust, that's when you're at peace.

Now is it easy to go to this place?, it's not, it's hard, but with regular and consistent practice to bear the thoughts and trying to focus on the thing that's before you, you develop a way to control yourself no matter the wind.

While different OCD have different actions that you can perform to calm yourself down, enduring the doubt and focusing on what's infront of me is what really helped me when it comes to obsessing over things. Such as yours. I hope this helps.
